citations.description: Push loop still exits 1 after max_retries exhausted; backoff is exponential (anti-adaptive per ticket analysis) and unchanged.

Ticket Phase 1 comment: 'Modes 2 and the marker over-match are being filed as linked follow-ups rather than bundled: mode 2 changes retry semantics of a shared push path and needs a contention harness.'

findings.criterion: Mode (2): the `origin/tickets` push either succeeds under normal contention (adequate retry/backoff, or fetch-rebase-retry) or exits non-red when it has provably lost a benign race.
findings.detail: The workflow's push-retry loop still terminates with `exit 1` after exhausting 5 retries (reconcile-bridge.yml line 334-335). The ticket's own Phase 1 comment explicitly defers Mode 2 to a follow-up ticket, stating 'Modes 2 and the marker over-match are being filed as linked follow-ups rather than bundled.' No code change makes the push exit non-red on benign contention exhaustion, and no follow-up ticket is linked in the deps. The AC requires either adequate retry/backoff that succeeds OR a non-red exit on a provably benign race — neither is implemented.

citations.description: Ticket comments contain only the Phase 1 root-cause analysis; no post-fix measurement window or gh run list output is present.

findings.criterion: Measured: over a comparable window (>= 500 runs) after the fix, the `Reconcile Bridge` failure count attributable to modes (1) and (2) is zero, evidenced by `gh run list`.
findings.detail: This criterion requires a live production measurement (>= 500 runs post-fix) with evidence from `gh run list`. No such attestation appears in the ticket comments or anywhere in the repository. The ticket status is `in_progress` and no post-fix run inventory has been recorded.
findings.remediation: Record a `gh run list` output (or equivalent Actions API summary) as a ticket comment once >= 500 runs have accumulated after the fix lands, showing zero failures attributable to modes (1) and (2). Include the run window timestamps and the raw counts.

citations.description: Ticket body: '124 pre-fix + 81 post-fix runs were cancelled (~15% of all runs), consistent with heavy schedule/dispatch overlap.' No follow-up explanation or reduction is recorded anywhere in the ticket comments or codebase.

findings.criterion: Cancellation rate is either explained as expected or reduced.
findings.detail: No code change, documentation, or ticket comment addresses the cancellation rate criterion. The ticket body notes ~15% cancellation as 'consistent with heavy schedule/dispatch overlap' and includes it 'as evidence rather than as a separate ticket', but neither the codebase nor the ticket comments record a formal explanation that it is expected, nor any reduction. The AC requires one of these two outcomes to be demonstrably satisfied.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
